analysis.title: If Losing Jensen Can't Sink Stocks, What Will? Pasquariello Says Watch The Fed In 2027
key_insights: Week of Nov 9-13, 2026: Nvidia lost its only CEO (Jensen Huang departed effective immediately) and shed over $500bn of market cap, ending the week down 13%, its worst week since April 2025. Core CPI was hot for a third straight month and the 2-year yield rose 33 bps. The Nasdaq 100 still rallied 3.5%.

Pasquariello (GS head of global hedge fund coverage) says risk/reward skews positive for the rest of 2026. His four reasons are technicals (position cleansing, supportive near-term flows), seasonals, AI demand, and above-trend nominal US GDP growth that appears to be accelerating in the second half.
Seasonal: since 1952 the last seven weeks of the year are up 69% of the time, for an average rally of 2.1%, now that the midterms are behind us.

Positioning: since the start of October the market absorbed a very large liquidation of risk, in both net and gross exposure. GS prime brokerage saw the biggest sale of global AI stocks in four years last week, and net exposure across the PB book is in the 3rd percentile of the past year.

Corporate bid: Pasquariello expects corporate supply-vs-demand to improve meaningfully as November progresses. Most of the S&P is out of the buyback blackout window, and 2026 buyback authorizations are a record $1.5 trillion.

2027 'sets up to be more complicated.' The AI buildout, which he calls the largest infrastructure project in US history, went right for four years because it was consistently bigger than expected and uninterrupted. The market has priced the first factor. The second is at risk from US politicians (data center moratoria, more regulation, higher taxes).

Inflation is his most important 2027 risk: core inflation is sticky and the latest CPI report suggests it is broadening. He says bull markets typically die because the central bank chokes off liquidity.

The third straight hot core CPI landed hours after Fed governor Waller floated a 50bp hike. The 2-year had its worst weekly backup (about 35 bps by Friday) since October 2024, all three coupon auctions tailed, and the 10-year is above 5.15%. Goldman economists added a third rate hike to their forecast.
Supply: 2027 will likely see the largest increase in net equity supply since 2000 (GS note exhibits 6 and 14), alongside a mega-IPO pipeline headlined by Anthropic.
Pasquariello's counterweights: NDX is on track to be up in 17 of the past 18 years on total returns, and sturdy GDP growth implies healthy earnings growth.

His conclusion: the balance of risks is positively skewed through year-end and the primary trend in the S&P remains higher. As 2026 becomes 2027 he expects more volatility, less upward convexity and lower risk-adjusted returns, 'more of a seesaw' with modest gains.

His framing has shifted week to week: Oct 19 he saw the tech dump as clearing the decks for a year-end rally, a week later he was 'licking my wounds', last week 'one last push higher before the turn', this week 'a seesaw'.

Credit: he was surprised by how many responses to last week's mention of US credit market concerns came back with significant negativity. Last week he relayed that two people he respects think stocks are too sanguine relative to credit.
The US economy has never been more sensitive to the stock market performance (exhibit 11), so a Fed hiking into hot CPI is also hiking into the biggest driver of consumer spending.

Chart: the S&P broke above the top of its five-year channel during the Q2 'mini bubble' and this month's selloff took it back to that line, where it held. The one-year rate of change has faded to roughly 12% from above 30% earlier in the year.
SOX had its best week since April as money rotated from Nvidia into AMD and Broadcom. Retail bought 41x more Nvidia than normal on the news.
CoreWeave rose on a beat and raise, but guided to a $1.1 billion quarterly interest bill with debt at $47 billion. TSMC and CoreWeave are cited by Pasquariello as evidence of strong AI demand.

The author's view (ZeroHedge, not Goldman) is that the path into year-end is probably higher, but the Fed, not a seesaw, more likely decides 2027. Next tests are Nvidia earnings on Tuesday, its first without Huang, and the Dec 9 FOMC.

risk_factors: Fed hikes into sticky, broadening core inflation, with Waller floating 50bp and GS adding a third hike.
Largest net equity supply increase since 2000 in 2027, plus a mega-IPO pipeline including Anthropic.
Political and regulatory disruption of the AI infrastructure buildout (data center moratoria, higher taxes).
US credit market concerns, with clients negative and stocks seen as too sanguine relative to credit.
The wealth effect now drives consumer spending, so a stock decline would feed back into the economy, a loop that is untested on the downside.
Leaders' departure and rotation risk: Nvidia's first earnings without Huang on Tuesday.
Treasury auction tails and a 10-year above 5.15%.
charts_described: Chart from GS and Bloomberg: top pane shows the S&P in the Covid/post-Covid era with the bullish trend intact and Q2 a 'mini bubble'. The lower pane shows the one-year rate of change, now about 12% versus above 30% earlier in the year.
vol_and_positioning: GS PB book net exposure is in the 3rd percentile versus the past year.

US fundamental L/S gross leverage fell 8.7 points in a single week, the biggest hedge fund degross since Covid. Net leverage hit the 0th percentile on a five-year lookback (cited from an earlier ZeroHedge piece).
Last week GS saw the biggest sale of global AI stocks since 2022.
The S&P equal-weight index closed Friday about 1% from all-time highs.
Daily rotations within the market have been brutal, especially for leveraged participants.
Retail bought 41x more Nvidia than normal after the CEO news.
Pasquariello expects more volatility and less upward convexity in 2027.
geopolitical: US political risk to the AI buildout: after the midterms (a 'blue wave'), data center moratoria are on the table, plus risk of more regulation and higher taxes.
cross_bank_references: Goldman's own economists added a third rate hike, which the author contrasts with Pasquariello's positive year-end skew.
Pasquariello points to Peter Oppenheimer's GS global portfolio strategy team for the house view on the year ahead.

tension_points.bull_case: Light positioning (3rd percentile net), friendly seasonals (up 69% of the time since 1952), a record $1.5 trillion buyback bid, above-trend nominal GDP and NDX up in 17 of 18 years.
tension_points.bear_case: Sticky and broadening core inflation, a Fed hiking (Waller floated 50bp, GS adds a third hike), the largest net equity supply since 2000, political risk to the AI buildout and a credit market that is worrying clients.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The author says the Fed decides the outcome. The first tests are Nvidia earnings on Tuesday and the Dec 9 FOMC.

tension_points.bull_case: Fresh evidence that AI demand remains insatiable, citing TSMC and CoreWeave's beat and raise.
tension_points.bear_case: The upside surprise is priced and the uninterrupted path is at risk from US politicians. CoreWeave guided to $1.1 billion in quarterly interest with $47 billion of debt.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Data center moratoria or more regulation and higher taxes after the midterms.
